items.statement: PG expansion phase 1 of 32,000 MT/annum at Rs 94 crore with 50:50 debt-equity and 20.7% IRR
items.quote: The first one is the propylene glycol plants with an initial phase one capacity of 32,000 metric ton per annum. The model investment is for 94 crores with a 50 :50 Debt Equity ratio has an IRR of 20.7%.

items.statement: Polyester polyol plant 1 of 4,150 MT/annum completed; plant 2 expected by end of Q3 or beginning of Q4 FY25
items.quote: Two such plants are planned and 1 is already completed with the 4,150 MT per annum capacity and the second one it's an ongoing project we'll be focusing at construction and appliances and elastomers specifically with polyester polyol coupled with the captive consumption requirement.

items.statement: West India Greenfield expansion approved for 30,000 MT/annum polyols at Rs 130+ crore with 30% IRR and 5-year payback
items.quote: The board has recently approved an expansion into West India to cater to the requirements of the local market. Initially, we will target 30,000 tons per annum of polyols with an investment model of 130 plus crores and IRR of 30% is projected with the five-year payback.

items.statement: PG expansion phase 1 to complete in Q2 FY25; volumes to ramp in stages
items.quote: We should be completing the project in Q2 of FY 2025. So immediately from there on, we should be focusing more on marketing the additional capacities what we have.

items.statement: Plant 1 utilisation fell from 82% to 72%; Plant 2 from 55% to 45% (FY22 to FY24), in line with global rates
items.quote: Global operation rate went down from 82% to about 65, if you look at your company from 2021-22 to 2023-2024, for Plant 1, we went from 82% to 72% for Plant 2, we went from 55% to 45 %.

items.statement: Margins stressed by China slowdown, import dumping, raw material cost, supply chain disruptions, Cyclone Michaung; back to pre-COVID levels
items.quote: The slowdown in China has significantly increased imports into India, putting lot of pressure on our NRVs, especially slab stock. The increased raw material cost coupled with supply chain disruptions, increased transportation costs the month or so impact of Cyclone Michaung in December 23. All these have put a tremendous stress on our margins.

items.statement: Propylene (70% of RM) priced monthly by state-owned entities based on butane/propane and crude; no pricing power over input cost
items.quote: Our major raw material is propylene which is you know 70% of our consumption. That depends on the price of butane and propane and the international market price of crude so obviously you know it fluctuates on a monthly basis and it's fixed by the government entities which supplies our raw materials.

items.statement: Global petrochemical operating rates bottomed in 2022; recovery from China not expected soon; cycle to continue 1-1.5 years
items.quote: We are definitely looking at the recovery from China and we do not expect that recovery to come anytime soon. So, for us, we feel that we have reached the bottom of the cycle, but we don't feel that we are yet in a place where we are going to see a very strong growth.

items.statement: India manufacturing growth, public investment, luxury real estate driving demand; FTA with UAE bringing petrochemical capacity
items.quote: Manufacturing sector has definitely been growing a lot. Public investment has been coming into India more and more. Luxury residential, real estate have been one of the key drivers for the country growth.

items.statement: Consolidated portfolio: 63% commodities, 37% specialties; PG 27%, slab stock 19%, others 31% (Thermo Ware, General Rigids, Coal cure modes, Notedome, PennWhite)
items.quote: If we look at the product wise portfolio, propylene glycol stand stop at 27% of the overall portfolio followed by sla b stock at 19%, the others of 31% includes our Thermo Ware , General Rigids, Coal cure modes, No tedome and PennWhite products as well.

items.statement: If ADD on China/Thailand slab stock polyol imposed, polyol share could rise from 19% to 30-35% (60% of imports from China/Thailand)
items.quote: If the government is supportive of this ADD predominantly, I would say 60% of the imports which come from China and Thailand and the balance 40% from Singapore, that will certainly you know, improve our share of the product portfolio from 19%, it could go even up to 30-35%.

items.statement: PG industrial and fragrance grades facing dumping, pressuring NRVs; sole PO manufacturer in India, market leader in PG, polyols, PGMME, only integrated polyol maker
items.quote: On the PG segment , on the industrial grade and fragrance grade, there is a dumping happening now. So, the market is facing pressure on the NRV's because of the dumping on these two segments of PG.

items.statement: Long-term debt very low; strong liquidity ~Rs 400 crore by end Jun 2024; CARE A+(stable) long-term, A1+ short-term rating
items.quote: We are A+(stable)credit rating from CARE for our long-term borrowings and A1+ for short term borrowings. Our long-term debt is very low and we have a strong liquidity of around 400 crores by end of June 24.

items.statement: Consolidated current ratio 4.3, quick ratio 3.6; FY24 consolidated revenue Rs 1,061 crore
items.quote: We have 4.3 presently on the current ratio and 3.6 on the quick ratio, we clocked the top line of INR 1,061 crores consolidated for the previous financial year 23 -24.

items.statement: 10-year unbroken dividend record; 15% dividend declared for FY24 despite tough conditions; focus on maintaining dividends
items.quote: We continue to maintain a 10-year unbroken record on dividend declaration and in spite of tough situation for the financial year 2023-24, we had declared a 15% dividend to the shareholders.

items.statement: PennWhite acquired 2 years ago; establishing Indian subsidiary with first employees doing business development; assessing manufacturing hub in India for domestic and Asian markets
items.quote: We are actively asses sing the opportunities to create a manufacturing hub based in India, not just producing for the Indian market, but potentially also for the wider Asian region.

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.98% in Q2 from 3.97% and 3.92% in prior quarters; Net interest income grew 15% YoY with INR 375 crore addition
items.quote: Net interest income has also seen a good growth of 15% Y-o-Y, with an addition of INR 375 crore. NIM has also seen improvement and has grown 3.98% from 3.97% and 3.92% in the last 2-3 quarters.

items.statement: Gold loan portfolio at INR 13,000 crore, targeting minimum INR 15,000 crore by year-end; co-lending book reached nearly INR 2,000 crore with 6-7 NBFC partnerships
items.quote: My portfolio has already touched INR 13,000 crore. By end of the year, we plan to take it to minimum INR 15,000 crore, which I see is quite achievable. We have also done some co-lending partnerships with leading gold loan NBFCs.

items.statement: Co-lending book reached almost INR 2,000 crore with 6-7 NBFC partnerships rated AA and above; another 3-4 under discussion
items.quote: This co-lending has gone up to almost INR 2,000 crore we are reaching. For this, we have identified Bank of Maharashtra October 15, 2024 NBFCs rated AA and above , and we have seen how the processes and how the audit system, how the compliance levels are getting maintained

items.statement: GNPA improved to 1.84% from 2.19% YoY; NNPA at 0.2%; PCR at 98.31%; total recovery INR 475 crore in Q2 (cash INR 120 cr, upgradation INR 100 cr, write-off recovery INR 255 cr)
items.quote: GNPA has improved and has come down to 1.84% against 2.19% last year. NNPA is at 0.2%. Recovery has also been good in Q2 with cash recovery of INR 120 crore, upgradation around INR 100 crore and write-off recovery of INR 255 crore, we have a total recovery of INR 475 crore.

items.statement: SMA book at 5.8% (down from 7.54% YoY); excluding 4-5 state entity accounts (INR 1,542 cr), stress at 5.09%; SMA-2 only 2 accounts below INR 60 cr each
items.quote: If you see year-on-year, it was 7.54%, and now we are at 5.8%. I'm talking about the total. Not SMA-2, but the SMA and the total position for the bank within which 5.8%, what I've said, it is a few of the state entity accounts, 4-5 accounts, which has actually moved to the SMA category, and INR 1,542 crore are in these 5 accounts.

items.statement: Slippage ratio maintained at INR 500-600 crore per quarter; credit cost below 0.40% per month on IRAC basis; net NPA 0.20%
items.quote: Regarding slippage ratio, you can see that we are able to maintain slippage in quantum term roughly around INR 600 crore which will continue in future also. The slippage will be within the range of INR 500 crore to INR 600 crore.

items.statement: RAM loans grew high double-digits: Retail 23%, Agriculture 34% (driven by gold loans), MSME 25% YoY; Corporate grew 9% YoY
items.quote: Coming to the RAM side, in the loan book all the 3 parameters, Retail, Agri, MSME have seen a high double-digit growth of 23% Y-o-Y in Retail. Agriculture, 34%, wherein large part of contribution has come from agricultural gold loans. MSME has also seen a Y-o-Y growth of 25%.

items.statement: Private capex cycle not yet visible in real terms; green shoots appearing, utilization of sanctioned limits increasing; expect traction in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Yet I think that private capex cycle in real term is not yet visible. But we are seeing some green shoots are there. In some sectors, things are only moving up. Traction is visible.

items.statement: Board approved 5-year plan to open 1,000 branches; 600 opened in last 3 years; targeting 200-220 branches in next 12 months
items.quote: We have, in fact, gone to our Board with a 5-year roadmap, 1,000 branches is what we have envisaged. The Board has approved this plan of ours, which is 1,000 branches in the next 5 years. Around 600 branches were opened in the Bank of Maharashtra October 15, 2024 last 3 years

items.statement: IT budget INR 1,000 crore for current year; INR 2,700 crore budget over last 3 years with INR 1,900 crore utilized; 138 RFPs floated; hardware refresh completion by February 2025
items.quote: So, in all the areas, we have done, actually, right now, still this year, we are having a budget of around INR 1,000 crore. But the pace of that RFPs will not continue to that extent because in all the areas we have floated the RFPs and all the projects are going on, most of them are completed, and it will take 6 months to 9 months' time to get the result.

items.statement: Raised INR 3,500 crore equity via QIP, INR 811 crore infrastructure bonds, INR 1,000 crore Tier 2 bonds recently
items.value: INR 3,500 crore equity, INR 811 crore infra bonds, INR 1,000 crore Tier 2
items.quote: Also recently we have raised INR 3,500 crore equity capital as well as the infrastructure bond at INR 811 crore. We have also raised Tier 2 bond of INR 1,000 crore.

items.statement: CASA grew 12% YoY, added INR 15,000 crore absolute; CASA ratio maintained at guidance level of ~50%
items.quote: CASA has grown Y-o-Y by 12%. In terms of absolute number, we have added INR 15,000 crore of CASA in our book. The ratio stands at our level of guidance, which is to maintain it around 50%, and that's the CASA ratio with the bank.

items.statement: CD ratio at 78.72% against guidance of 79-80%; CET1 at 12%, CRAR at 17.26%; ROA 1.74% (up 36 bps YoY), ROE 26.01%
items.quote: The CD ratio, is being maintained at the desirable level of 78.72% against our guidance of maintaining it around 79%-80% levels.

items.statement: Agriculture portfolio INR 8,000 crore, of which INR 5,000 crore from gold loans; KCC growth only 6% vs agri gold loans 29% YTD; centralized underwriting for KCC at zonal level
items.value: INR 8,000 crore total, INR 5,000 crore gold
items.quote: Agriculture portfolio has grown to INR 8,000 crore, out of which INR 5,000 crore have come from gold loan alone.

items.statement: Unsecured personal loans INR 3,350 crore (salary/pension tied-up only), GNPA only INR 15 crore (0.05%); no unsecured lending to non-salaried
items.quote: So, to say that this personal loan segment put together this pension and other things, it is INR 3,350 crore, and only INR 15 crore is NPA out of that. So it's a high-yielding product for me, and it is very much in focus.

items.statement: Corporate book at 38-39% of gross advances; maintaining RAM vs Corporate at 60-40 +/-2%; no strategic decision to lower corporate exposure; targeting PLI, infra, renewable sectors
items.quote: Today, we have kept the guidance of RAM versus Corporate at 60 - 40, and plus/minus 2%. Currently, we are looking at the sector's proposals, which are coming Bank of Maharashtra October 15, 2024 from the upcoming sectors, the infra, the renewable energy and the like

items.statement: Applied for GIFT City license; Board approved; awaiting regulator approval for ECB and global syndication opportunities
items.quote: Currently, we are mindful of the fact that there is a GIFT City opportunity with us. We have already gone to the Board, and the Board has approved our proposal post which we have submitted our request to the regulator, and we will be in discussions with the regulator and pursuing our case with them to give us the GIFT City license as early as possible.

items.statement: Liquidity comfortable with sizable SLR portfolio; INR 40,000 crore total liquidity (CRR + SLR); CD ratio 78.72% shows well-managed liquidity
items.quote: CRR, we are having, SLR we are having, so around I think INR 20,000 crore, INR 25,000 crore, total INR 40,000 crore is existing liquidity.

items.statement: No exposure to MTNL and RINL; NCLT write-off book INR 21,000 crore (INR 8,800 crore NCLT, INR 5,100 crore resolved); expect INR 1,500 crore recovery from resolved NCLT cases this year
items.quote: We have also with us INR 21,000 crore of write-off book, within which the NCLT is almost INR 8,800 crore. Out of INR 8,800 crore, INR 5,100 crore is already where the resolution has come, whether liquidation order has come to me or the RA has been declared under NCLT as a successful bidder.

items.statement: Digital business zone nearing INR 5,000 crore business with zero employees; 60 RPA implemented, Board approval for 150; 12-15 STP journeys launched, 5 in CUG state
items.quote: Now that zone is nearing INR 5,000 crore approximately as o f today. So, it is between INR 4,500 crore to INR 4,700 crore. So here, no employee is actually involve d in the business, and through only digital they have an entire setup like a physical zone

items.statement: Co-lending NIM 5%+ in some arrangements; PSL targets met via co-lending enabling PSLC sales at 1.5-2% additional yield
items.quote: I have been able to find a very good pricing which we have been able to negotiate in terms of service. Through this technology, we are able to give good services, add value in the partnership and I'm able to, in return, get good pricing. My NIM typically in some arrangements is 5% plus.

items.statement: More than 50% presence outside Maharashtra; last 3 years branch expansion outside Maharashtra; 1,000 branch plan focused on new growth centers outside Maharashtra
items.quote: First of all, there is some misconception around that. We are not predominantly in Maharashtra. I think more than 50% of our presence is outside Maharashtra. If you ask me last 3 years, the new branch opening has been outside Maharashtra.

items.statement: Sanctions of INR 39,000 crore in H1 FY25 (INR 30,000 crore corporate); visibility to achieve 18%+/-2% advance growth
items.quote: So far in the first half year itself, we have made sanctions of around INR 39,000 crore, of which around INR 30,000 crore pertains to corporate credit segment.

items.statement: MoRTH disqualified PNC Infratech and two SPVs from participating in any MoRTH tender process for one year effective 18 Oct 2024
items.quote: vide its Order dated 18 th October 2024 MoRTH has disqualified the Company and the two SPVs from participating in any tender process of the Ministry for a period of 1 year with effect from 18th October 2024.

items.statement: Gross order book stands at over Rs 21,000 crores including three new projects worth Rs 6,670 crores awarded by MSRDC and CIDCO
items.quote: Including the value of above three new projects, the Company's gross order book as on date is over Rs. 21,000 crores, without deducting the value of execution done during the second quarter ending 30 September 2024.

items.statement: Management maintains order inflow guidance for FY25 and will provide firm numbers at Q2 results in November
items.quote: So, as of now, we want to maintain the same order book guidance. Going forward, in the month of November when we declare Q2 results and we will have a concall, then we will be able to tell you more firm numbers and more kind of concrete changes.

items.statement: Disqualification applies only to MoRTH, NHAI and NHIDCL; other central ministries and state governments remain accessible for bidding
items.quote: As the Company has been disqualified from tender process for period of one year of the MoRTH only, the Company is able to continue to pursue business opportunities with the other central ministries and various authorities/agencies of the state governments and accordingly should be able to participate in tender processes.

items.statement: Three new major projects awarded for aggregate contract value of Rs 6,670 crores from MSRDC and CIDCO
items.quote: As we had intimated to the exchanges, the Company has recently been awarded three new major projects for an aggregate contract value of Rs. 6,670 crores; two projects by MSRDC and one project by CIDCO.

items.statement: Ongoing CBI case has not yet reached trial stage; designated court has not taken cognizance or framed charges
items.quote: the designated court has not taken cognizance of the matter and also not framed the charges, and the trial has not begun.

items.statement: Only three entities disqualified; other subsidiaries can bid for MoRTH projects if they qualify independently
items.quote: Yes, only three companies are disqualified. If other subsidiary qualified for the other project then we can bid.

items.statement: Robust unexecuted order book provides revenue visibility over next two to two and a half years
items.quote: The above robust unexecuted order book shows a tangible revenue visibility over the next two to two & half years.

items.statement: KKR asset monetization not expected to be affected by disqualification order; buyer aware of developments
items.quote: No, to our best of understanding, we don't think that it will get affected and seeking NOCs from the government as well as since the buyer is also aware of all these developments which are in the public domain, we don't take any deviations would be there from the present course of action.

items.statement: Existing projects including those with appointed date awaited and five HAM projects will not be impacted by disqualification order
items.quote: That part will not be affected.

items.statement: Management evaluating all legal options to minimize and mitigate impacts of disqualification order
items.quote: Nonetheless, we are evaluating all the resources available to the Company including legal actions that can be taken by the Company to minimise and mitigate the impacts of the said Order on the Company's performance going forward.

items.statement: No grant payments pending for the two SPVs; only change in law payments (GST) may be receivable
items.quote: See, there is no grant in these SPVs because the grant completes once the project is commissioned during the construction time, no grant is pending, and as of now no annuities are also pending. But maybe there are certain payments under change in law which we will be getting.

items.statement: Disqualification order limited to tender participation only; does not affect ongoing development, construction, O&M activities or annuity receipts
items.quote: there will not be any impact on the ongoing development, construction, operation & maintenance activities of the Company and its subsidiaries including the said two SPVs on account of the aforesaid Order.

items.statement: Management will share details on bids submitted to NHAI/MoRTH with pending outcomes and further order inflow visibility at Q2 results in November
items.quote: we submitted a couple of bids, we will share it separately because currently we don't have the information.

items.statement: JFL loan book reached Rs 1,206 crore as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: Jio Finance Ltd, or JFL, our NBFC. A diverse array of products are now available for retail and corporate customers, through JFL, which has built a loan book of 1,206 crores as on September 30, 2024.

items.statement: JPBL CASA customer base increased to 1.5 million
items.quote: Jio Payments Bank Ltd., or JPBL. JPBL continued to offer convenient savings bank account-related services to Indians and increased the base of CASA customers to 1.5 million.

items.quote: Regarding our JV with BlackRock for investment solutions, we are very happy to share that on October 3 rd, 2024, the regulator has granted JFSL and BlackRock in -principle approval to sponsor a mutual fund, subject to certain customary requirements being fulfilled

items.statement: DEA approved increase in foreign investment limit to 49% of paid-up equity share capital on fully diluted basis
items.quote: Further, the Company received approval from Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance to increas e the aggregate limit for foreign investment s in the company, including foreign portfolio investment, up to 49% of its paid -up equity share capital on a fully diluted

items.statement: Consolidated total income Rs 694 crore, profit after tax Rs 689 crore for Q2 FY25
items.quote: For Q2 FY25, the company reported a total consolidated income of Rs. 694 crores and a profit after tax of Rs 689 crores.

items.statement: Consolidated total expenses Rs 146 crore including Rs 4 crore provisions in Q2 FY25
items.quote: The company's total expenses during the quarter, including provisions of Rs. 4 crores, was Rs. 146 crores, as compared to Rs. 71 Crores in the year-ago period, and Rs. 79 crores in the first quarter of FY25.

items.statement: Standalone profit after tax Rs 305 crore for Q2 FY25 vs Rs 72 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: On a standalone basis, the profit after tax of the company during the quarter was Rs.305 crores, as compa red to Rs. 72 crores for the preceding quarter, and Rs 89 crores in the corresponding quarter last year

items.statement: Invested Rs 68 crore in JPBL to increase holding from 78.95% to 82.17%
items.quote: During the quarter under review, the company invested Rs.68 crore s in the payments bank, JPBL, to increase its holding from 78.95% to 82.17

items.statement: JLSL invested Rs 67.50 crore in RILIL
items.quote: Also, our leasing services subsidiary, JLSL, invested Rs.67.50 crores in RILIL.

items.statement: Launched Home Loans, Loan Against Property, UPI International, Account Aggregator, biometric payments, credit card billers in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In Q2, we have added many more products, such as Home Loans (including Balance Transfer), Loan Against Property, UPI International, Account Aggregator for multiple bank accounts and mutual fund ho ldings, biometric -enabled payments, and addition of credit card billers for leading banks

items.statement: JIBL now offers 24 insurance plans digitally across life, health, two-wheeler and motor insurance through 31 insurance providers
items.quote: JIBL is now offering as many as 24 insurance plans digitally across life, health, two-wheeler and motor insurance, directly to customers through the JioFinance app and the website jioinsure.in.

items.statement: JioFinance app reached around 6.5 million users; MyJio integration completed in Q2 FY25
items.quote: I am very happy to report that around 6.5 million users experienced JFSL's new-age financial services on our digital platforms, and these numbers are only growing as we speak.

items.statement: JIBL onboarded large and mid corporates in institutional channel; launched employee benefit portal
items.quote: With respect to institutional channel, the growth momentum has been encouraging with the onboarding of some large and mid corporates, and employee benefit portal was also launched during the quarter for these institutional clients.

items.statement: Incorporated Jio Finance Platform and Service Limited (wholly owned) and Jio BlackRock Investment Advisers Private Limited (50:50 JV)
items.quote: During the quarter under review, two new entities were incorporated: Jio Finance Platform and Service Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary, for distribution of financial products and allied services, and, Jio BlackRock Investment Advisers Private Limited, a 50:50 JV with BlackRock which will provide investment advisory services, subject to regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Consolidated net worth Rs 1.37 lakh crore, total assets Rs 1.44 lakh crore, total investments Rs 1.37 lakh crore as of September 30, 2024
items.quote: JFSL’s consolidated net worth stood at Rs.1.37 lakh crores as on September 30 th, 2024. Consolidated total assets stood at Rs. 1.44 lakh crores, with consolidated total investments of Rs. 1.37 lakh crores

items.statement: Share of Associates & Joint Ventures increased to Rs 225 crore in Q2 FY25 from Rs 218 crore in Q2 FY24 and Rs 62 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Share of Associates & Joint ventures increased to Rs 225 crores in Q2 FY25 from Rs 218 crores in the corresponding period of FY24, and Rs. 62 crores in the first quarter of FY25.

items.statement: Confident of sustaining product launch momentum with new products rolled out over successive quarters
items.quote: Going forward, we are confident of sustaining this momentum with new products being ruled out, rolled out, over the successive quarters.

items.statement: Will further strengthen digital distribution through JioFinance app and MyJio, leverage data analytics for customer targeting
items.quote: Along with that, we will also further strengthen the digital distribution of products and services through JioFinance app and MyJio, reaching out to new customers.

items.statement: Employee cost and other operating expenses increased pursuant to scaling up of operations
items.quote: This was largely on account of increase in employee cost, and other operating expenses pursuant to scaling up of our operations.

items.statement: JioFinance app Beta launched May 30, 2024; new improved version rolled out October 10, 2024
items.quote: We launched a Beta of the app on May 30, 2024, and ran a campaign thereafter to gather customer feedback, which was used to further enhance the user experience of the app. The result of this entire exercise is the new and improved JioFinance app rolled out on October 10th.

items.statement: JPSL upcoming features include NEFT and RTGS payment solutions for B2B invoice payments and Brand EMIs
items.quote: In the pipeline for JPSL, upcoming features such as NEFT and RTGS payment solutions for B2B invoice payments and Brand EMIs are on the roadmap.

items.statement: Demand for all forms of financial services remains encouraging to support growth aspirations of young and growing country
items.quote: The Indian economy remains resilient and has exhibited robust growth. To support the growth aspirations of young and growing country, the demand for all forms of financia l services remains encouraging

items.statement: JPBL expanding Business Correspondents network across the country; base being scaled up further
items.quote: JPBL is also making steady progress in terms of expanding its Business Correspondents, or BC network across the country with a base of [LOST AUDIO] being scaled up further as we speak.

items.statement: Expect tea prices to remain elevated until Q1 next year; more staggered price increases coming
items.quote: Tea prices remain elevated. I would say you could expect to see that getting into quarter 1 of next year. And therefore , staggered price increases have been a ctioned and you will see more price increases around the corner

items.statement: Expect NourishCo to return to 25-30% growth by end of current quarter
items.quote: And we do expect -- I would say, by end of this quarter, we should be back to our 25%, 30% growth levels.

items.statement: Will structurally improve margins year-on-year; at lowest end of FMCG sector with long way to go
items.quote: But fundamentally, we will improve margins year-on-year. We are at the lowest end of the FMCG sector in terms of -- while we have improved from where we've come from, we've still got a long way to go to come up to, I would say, benchmarks in the food and beverage sector.

items.statement: Rural recovering with good monsoon; urban softened due to food inflation and government capex pause
items.quote: I think a good monsoon and therefore, the Kharif crop is only going to help in the rural recovery, but it is still not at the stage where it gives us a double-digit volume growth and the penetration growth, etc. But while this has happened, urban has softened.

items.statement: Tea volumes declined year-on-year for first time in long time; salt volume growth slowed to 1% from 8% last quarter
items.quote: India Beverages up 3% with tea volumes actually declining year-on-year. Just as a perspective, I think this is probably after a long, long time, we have seen a decline in tea volumes.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin contracted 30 bps to 14.9% due to higher tea input costs; tea costs up 25-30%
items.quote: Consolidated EBITDA grew 11%. Margin actually contracte d 30 bps to 14.9%, primarily led by higher input costs for the India tea business. As a perspective, tea costs have gone up by about 25% to 30

items.statement: Salt margin largely mitigated with price increase; tea margin recovery depends on competitive environment
items.quote: For salt I think more or less we miti gated the cost increase. So that is done. You could see us maintaining/inching up slightly the margin. I would say no significant movement

items.statement: Tea costs up 25-30%; staggered price increases taken but not fully passed on; more increases coming
items.quote: As a perspective, tea costs have gone up by about 25% to 30%, and we expect them to stay elevated for some points of time. While we have taken gradual tea price increases, we have not so far passed on the entire tea cost increase to the consumer.

items.statement: Announced INR2 price increase on Tata Salt (INR28 base) effective October to mitigate Mithapur rain impact
items.quote: We did have impact on cost for salt because Mithapur recorded its highest ever rain since 1929. And in line with mitigating the cost increase, we've announced a INR2 price increase, which will start getting into the market this month.

items.statement: Capital Foods quarter-on-quarter grew 25% to INR206 crores; Organic India grew 45% to INR102 crores; combined 31% QoQ growth
items.quote: Overall, Organic India, INR102 crores, Capital Foods, INR206 crores, both put together a 31% quarter-on-quarter growth.

items.statement: Capital Foods distribution expanded from 250,000 to nearly 500,000 outlets; Organic India reached 400,000 households in Q2
items.quote: Capital Foods, we had taken over at about 250,000 outlets. It now reaches close to 500,000 outlets. Organic India also, we have started to move aggressively on growing the brand. Sampling is the key focus. We have reached about 400,000 outlet -- households in Q2.

items.statement: Growth businesses now 30% of TCPL India business; grew 15% organically (vs 30% target) due to NourishCo impact
items.quote: We had committed saying growth businesses will be 30%. Yes, we also said they'll be growing at 30%, which did not happen. But overall now, they are at a 30% contribution to TCPL [India] business. The growth businesses grew at 15%.

items.statement: Value-added salts grew 26%; Rock Salt scaling new heights monthly; Sampann grew 26%
items.quote: Value-added salts in line with their continued trajectory so far, continued to grow strong double-digit, grew 26%. Rock Salt continues to scale new heights every quarter. Sampann had a strong quarter, 26% growth.

items.statement: Modern trade grew 17%; e-commerce grew 50% with quick commerce very strong; 100% distributors on auto-replenishment and new DMS MAVIC
items.quote: Modern trade is now almost -- I mean continuing the trend. So the softness which you saw in the last quarter was primarily in general trade. Modern trade continued to deliver at 17% growth. E -commerce was 50% growth. And in e -commerce, we saw quick commerc e come in very, very strongly

items.statement: Food services and pharma channel pilots started in Mumbai, Ahmedabad and 10 cities; distributor appointment finishing this month
items.quote: Incubation of food services chan nel, which we had committed, we've started pilots in Mumbai and Ahmedabad and pharma channel across 10 cities, on both these things, we've started -- we're still not -- I would guess we will finish appointing all the distributors by end of this month, but initial results look quite encouraging

items.statement: NourishCo re-indexed pricing after 30% premium to competitor A and 20% to multinationals; loss of INR1.5-2 per bottle on Gluco+
items.quote: We were roughly about, I would say, ab out 30% premium to competitor A, and about 20% premium to the multinationals in terms of price to retail. Now just as a perspective, we know at that price to retail that is not sustainable, and the loss is roughly INR2 -- INR1.50 to INR2 per bottle

items.statement: Will not sacrifice market share for short-term profitability; competitive on tea pricing as competitors move
items.quote: Therefore, I will -- and I've maintained this earlier market share is a very, very important metric to me. Profitability is probably the next . Ideally, I would like to see both of them there . But therefore , we will make sure we are competitive out there and mo ve lockstep a s competitors move

items.statement: Starbucks added 19 stores to reach 457 stores across 70 cities; largest cafe operator in India
items.quote: Tata Starbucks is now the largest cafe operator in India with 457 stores across 70 cities.

items.statement: Starbucks same-store sales negative; stress across QSR sector due to urban consumption slowdown and food inflation
items.quote: Same-store sales is negative, and I think it is negative for the sector for now.

items.statement: Rights issue completed mid-Q2; bridge finance paid off; company now net cash positive at INR332 crores
items.quote: We finished the rights issue in the middle of Q2. And now as we exit the quarter, we are debt free, and therefore, there will be a positive impact from that perspective as we go forward.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds used to square off bridge finance for acquisitions; interest cost to come down significantly
items.quote: given that we have already squared off the bridge finance that we had taken for the acquisition, and this was done throug h the rights issue proceeds. We should now see significantly enhanced flow -through from EBIT to PBT as the interest cost comes down

items.statement: Innovation-to-sales ratio at 4.1% for quarter; on track for 5%+ for full year
items.quote: Innovation-to-sales ratio, we were at about 4.1% for the quarter. which is on track to -- for us to deliver a 5% plus for the full year.

items.statement: A&P-to-sales ratio maintained at 7.5% in India despite softness
items.quote: Despite the softness, we want to continue to strengthen our brands and our A&P-to-sales ratio in India continued at 7.5%.

items.statement: Solubles business seeing demand stress at stratospheric coffee prices; demand destruction term used by top roasters
items.quote: the catch is what we are seeing on the solubles piece is now demand softn ess. As the prices have reached those levels, I think now we are testing the boundaries I don't know if they will continue to go up sequentially because now what we are hearing across from a ll the top coffee roasters around is they are starting to -- when I see the word saying demand destruction being used, I know there is

items.statement: Tea volume stress expected if 30-35% price increases needed to pass on cost inflation
items.quote: on volumes. Volumes didn't go negative. There was immense stress, but there was no growth, if I may. I think you will probably see that scenario play out because if there is a 30%, 35% price increase, which will have to happen to translate this cost in, I do think you will start seeing stress on volume

items.statement: Merger of three wholly-owned subsidiaries completed with NCLT approval; one-off tax benefit from carry-forward losses
items.quote: We had NCLT approval, and therefore, we finished the merger of our wholly owned subsidiaries. And therefore, in line with that, you will also see a tax impact on our P&L because we had the advantage of offsetting so me of the accrued losses in the wholly owned subsidiary

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY25 is 75% to 100%
items.quote: So, we have already said between 75% to 100% for the entire year.

items.statement: FY26 guidance will be given by March 2025
items.quote: No, next year, I better give that guidance by March.

items.statement: Transaction processing grew ~20% in FY25, expected to exceed 15 billion transactions
items.quote: We have seen about 20% growth in transaction processing on our platform in this particular financial year. So, we are seeing that it will be more than 15 billion transactions that we will be processing.

items.statement: Secured Bharat Bill payment aggregation switch from two banks and one online dispute resolution order
items.quote: We secured Bharat Bill payment aggregation switch from two banks. And right now, it is in an operationalization stage, that's the quick update for the last quarter. We also secured one more order for the online dispute resolution from one of the banks.

items.statement: Added two sponsor banks; one in production CUG, one in pre-production; target 10 banks
items.quote: So, we added two sponsor banks, not just one. Looking at the last quarter, as soon as we realized that how quickly we'll have to get into this decision meticulously, we fast tracked it, we pushed all our focus on adding more banks. The vision is to add 10 banks.

items.statement: Two new banks (Kerala Gramin Bank and Karnataka Gramin Bank) to go live this quarter for super app

items.quote: I think you need to go through my balance sheet, and you should have also heard when I said that we have zero debt and we have had zero debt for almost about 5 -7 years now, we don't have any long-term debt.

items.statement: Temporary advance of ~US$7-8 lakh to Uzbekistan JV shown as loan asset
items.quote: As of September, it was around US$7 or US$8 lakh.

items.statement: No inorganic growth planned until top line crosses Rs 500 crore
items.quote: Not yet. I made the statement about a year and a half back. Let the company stabilize in the kind of growth target that we have set for ourselves . Once we cross 500 crores top line, then maybe we'll think of further diversification as of now.

items.statement: Uzbekistan JV: 600 hectares cotton seed production; harvest underway; may double if successful
items.quote: Uzbekistan, our joint venture has seen notable advancements with production of cotton seeds in over 600 hectares of land. Harvesting is currently underway, and we are optimistic about the results. Once successful, we may consider further expansion and extending the same strategy to neighboring countries overtime

items.statement: Philippines: trials successful; preparing for trial marketing; government sales could drive multi-year growth
items.quote: In Philippines, after successful trials we are currently preparing for trial marketing for our products in the upcoming season.

items.statement: Amol Gupta appointed CFO; Devinder Khurana moves to Senior VP role
items.quote: I would like to announce now that M r. Amol Gupta has taken over the charge of CFO from Dr. Devinder Khurana. Mr. Amol Gupta has been with the company for a few years now and was being mentored for the CFO role as the process of succession plan. Dr. Devinder Khurana will continue to be with the company as senior vice president of the company.

items.statement: Credit rating double upgraded from BBB- to BBB+; India Ratings upgraded, CRISIL review pending
items.quote: At the outset, I would like to inform you that our credit rating has seen a double upgradation from Triple B Minus to Triple B Plus. This is the confirmation of our operational stability.

items.statement: Disease-resistant okra and tomato hybrids command higher prices; require 2-3 molecular markers
items.quote: Our seeds which are getting emerged in okra as well as in tomato, are totally resistant. Our company has taken a policy that without appropriate markers, at least two to three markers, we should not reach hybrid. Similarly in rice also, we are ready with two products, Nath Bio-Genes Limited October 24, 2024 and we are going to come to the market. This indicates that we also get a better price for

items.statement: R&D spend Rs 9.37 crore last year, Rs 11.28 crore this year; using molecular markers and conventional breeding
items.quote: Last year it was 9.37 crores, this year it is 11.28 crores.

items.statement: Pan-India presence; 4,000-5,000 distributors; no government procurement schemes
items.quote: We have around 4 ,000 or 5 ,000 distributors all over the country and we just go through them. Every distributor has around 10 , 15 dealers and every dealer has around 15, 20, 25, 30 farmers. That's how the chain goes.

items.statement: Key competitors: Rasi, Kaveri, Nishabd Seeds, Mahyco (4-5 large players)
items.quote: Competitors like Rasi is our competitor, Kaveri is our competitor, Nishabd Seeds is our competitor or you can take Mahyco is our competitor. These are the 4-5 big companies who are competing with us.

items.statement: Land bank ~223 crore (revalued at Ind AS transition); 250-400 acres in Maharashtra for research/breeder seed
items.quote: Out of these 243 crores, the major chunk is land and not property and plant and equipment. Now that land is being used by the company for the search operation. I need land because I am a land-based company. So, the fixed assets are hardly 2-3 crores. The land itself is 223 crores.

items.statement: Philippines export timeline uncertain; depends on government trial results; not banking on it for growth
items.quote: Are we looking on Philippines for the company to grow? No, no. I have a domestic sales happening, I have domestic sales having capability of going beyond 500 and am I going to only rely up on Philippines to take the company forward? I think there is something missing. It is cherry on the cake.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue Rs 276.07 crore (+7% YoY); EBITDA Rs 42.18 crore; PAT Rs 36.78 crore; gross margin 51%
items.quote: H1 FY'25 top line clocked 276.07 crores, reflecting a growth of Y oY 7% as compared to H1 FY '24. The gross profit margin has been maintained at 51%. The EBITDA for the first half stands at 42.18 crores and the profit after tax is 36.78 crores.

items.statement: Medium-to-long-term AUM growth guidance of 20-25% maintained; may accept slightly lower growth in near term for asset quality
items.quote: Our medium -term to long -term growth guidance remains intact anywhere between 20% to 25%.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 assets expected to remain range-bound at 2.25-2.5%; net Stage 3 at 1.5-1.75%
items.quote: We would be happy if we can be in a position to manage anywhere between 2.25%, 2.5% on GNPAs. And net NPA end there between 1.5% to 1.75%.

items.statement: Gross Stage 3 assets rose marginally to 2.36% from 2.29% QoQ; net Stage 3 at 1.57%
items.quote: Talking to you about portfolio quality, it remained stable. That is INR2.36 crores gross Stage 3 asset as compared to INR2.29 crores gross Stage 3 asset in June quarter.

items.statement: Housing finance gross Stage 3 at 0.93% and net Stage 3 at 0.68% in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Here als o, the quality of the portfolio remains stable. That is gross Stage 3 asset is 0.93% as compared to 0.90% in June quarter and net Stage 3 asset is 0.68% as compared to 0.65% in June quarter.

items.statement: Housing finance GNPA expected to range 1-1.5% and NNPA 0.5-1% as portfolio matures
items.quote: We see that on -- as the portfolio matures and as the size increases the GNPAs will range anywhere between 1% to 1.5% and NNPA can be anywhere between 0.5% to 1%.

items.statement: SME rejection rates increased slightly due to overleveraging in some pockets; credit policies tightened
items.quote: One parameter, which helps us to look at this is that our rejection percentage has slightly gone up. So, our policies have been kept slightly tighter since some time.

items.statement: Stress seen across MEL, 2-wheeler, commercial vehicle segments; SME relatively benign
items.quote: The slight increase what we saw this time is evident from MEL 2-wheeler, commercial vehicle across segments because more or less, we start with the informal and the middle income and the lower income group of the society.

items.statement: Consolidated AUM grew 22.35% YoY to INR 11,681 crore; standalone AUM grew 21% YoY
items.quote: There is a growth of 22.35% in AUM on a consolidated basis. That is from INR9,547 crores to INR11, 681 crores.

items.statement: Housing finance AUM grew 32.67% YoY to INR 665 crore
items.quote: The AUM stands at INR665 crores. That is a growth of 32.67% from INR501 crores to INR665 crores.

items.statement: Commercial vehicle loans grew 62% YoY; salaried personal loans grew 84% YoY
items.quote: Commercial vehicle loan growth is 62%, around INR557 crores to INR900 crores. And salaried personal loans has a growth of 84%, INR372 crores to INR685 crores.

items.statement: Target mix: wheels ~25%, housing ~10%, PL <10%, rest SME and MEL
items.quote: Going forward, as I said earlier also that we would like wheels contribute around 25%, housing to contribute around 10% going forward, PL to contribute less than 10% and the rest to be contributed by SME and then the MEL that is the small business loan portfolio.

items.statement: MFI exposure reduced to <5% of AUM over last 6 quarters
items.quote: Since last 6 quarters or so, we have been progressively tapering our exposures on microfinance companies. As I talk to you currently, they form less than 5% of our total exposure on AUM for the on loans given to MFI.

items.statement: Branch count to increase from 198 to 215-220 by year-end; centers reach 13,000
items.quote: Currently, we have 198 branches, which will be anywhere between 215 to 220 branches by the year end. The centers reach has increased to 13,000.

items.statement: Direct distribution to reach 70-75% of sourcing in 3-4 years from current 66%
items.quote: Over the next three to four years, there's approximately 70/30 in favor of our retail distribution only because of the fact that the retail distribution will grow faster as compared to our NBFC distribution.

items.statement: BRE-enabled loan origination system to be implemented across products by end of Q3 FY25; full benefits from Q4
items.quote: I think by this quarter end we'll be in a position to implement a maturity of the product. But any new application is adopted, it takes its own time for full-fledged results. So I think within this quarter, it will be implemented. And within the next quarter, it will be yielding full-fledged results.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing stable at 9.83% in Q2 vs 9.80% in Q1; incremental borrowing at 9.75%; expected to remain same
items.quote: The cost of borrowing for the quarter was at 9.83%, the cost of borrowing for June quarter was 9.80%. The incremental borrowing which we did during the quarter is at around 9.75%. The cost of borrowing remains stable and we expect to remain at the same level in the coming quarter also.

items.statement: Capital adequacy at 26.52%, Tier 1 at 23.76%, debt-equity 3.25x; raised INR 660 cr term loans, INR 150 cr NCDs in Q2
items.quote: The capital adequacy remains strong at 26.52%, the tier 1 capital at 23.76% and debt equity of 3.25 times.

items.statement: Target 20-25% of AUM off-book via direct assignment and co-lending; currently at 21-22%
items.quote: The company aims to maintain around 20% to 25% of AUM as off book through direct assignment and co-lending partnerships.

items.statement: Capital market borrowing to increase from ~12% to 20% of liabilities in 3 years; ECB also planned
items.quote: Within the next 3 years, we intend that to take to 20% as a mark of our diversification with some contribution coming from ECB also that will give us a very well -diversified liability mix.

items.statement: Cash credit facility of INR 1,500 crore at 70-75% utilization; INR 950 cr average cash equivalents; INR 300 cr unutilized facilities
items.quote: We have available cash credit facility of around INR1,500 crores, out of which utiliz ation remains at around 70%, 75%, and rest portion kept as a liquidity buffer.

items.statement: Increasing supervisory oversight seen as short-term pain but long-term positive for orderly growth
items.quote: We all know that there is a lot of supervisory oversight in order to bring with an intention of the regulator to bring an orderly growth in the system, while it is a short-term pain, in the long term, it will bring about a more orderly growth.

items.statement: Consolidated headcount near 4,000; 500+ employees with >5 years tenure; in-house tech team of ~100
items.quote: We are -on a consolidated basis, we are close to now 4,000 persons working in the group. We continue to focus on getting higher efficiencies from them.

items.statement: ROA targeted at 2.8-3% range regardless of distribution channel mix
items.quote: Irrespective of the distribution channels, our ROAs will be range bound anywhere between say 2.8% to 3%.

items.statement: Branch breakeven may extend from 6-9 months to 12-15 months in current macro environment
items.quote: In current scenario where maybe things at a macro level are slightly slow, these 9 months can extend to, say, 12 or 15 months.

items.statement: Used vehicle loan vertical launch delayed to Q4 FY25 due to hiring challenges
items.quote: So we are rebuilding those -- that team. And I think we will start booking business as a special vertical from Q4, hopefully.

items.statement: Current installed capacity is 11,700 metric tons; expansion to 18,000 metric tons at Greater Noida plant is underway.
items.quote: Currently, our installed capacity is 11,700 metric tons, and we are looking to increase our capacity to about 18,000 metric tons with addition in the second unit, which is the Greater Noida plant.

items.statement: Capacity utilisation improved to 90-95% in H1 FY25 from 80-85% previously; expected to settle at 70-80% on the new 18,000-ton base by end of FY25.
items.quote: Currently, we are dealing with the capacity utilisation of about 90% to 95%. This has been possible because of better orders on the machinery, on the workstations that we have.

items.statement: Targets full utilisation of 18,000-ton capacity next financial year (FY26).
items.quote: that takes our capacity to 18,000 tons, which we are hoping to utilise on a full capacity basis in the next financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin increased 52% YoY and 39% half-yearly; PAT margin rose 49% on both YoY and HoH basis in H1 FY25.
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has increased because on a per kg basis, our EBITDA margins do not vary with the raw material or the sale prices. Hence, the margins on a percentage basis are increased to an extent of 52% YoY and 39% at half-yearly basis.

items.statement: Indian transformer market growing at 10-11% annually; demand rising from private sector (solar/wind) alongside government.
items.quote: We believe that the Indian transformer market is growing at about 10% to 11% on an annual basis, which is a very good growth rate considering our power sector.

items.statement: Order book of ₹62 crores as of 30 September, split ~50% power and ~40% distribution transformer cores.
items.quote: In terms of purchase orders, as of the end of 30th September, we had an order book of ₹62 crores, which comprised to almost 50% power and 40% distribution, transformer ports.

items.statement: Top five customers contribute 42% of revenue; key clients include Skipper, Supreme Power, Meiden, BHEL, Crompton Greaves; end customers include Power Grid, Adani Power, Indian Railways.
items.quote: Our top five customers consist of 42% of our total revenues.

items.statement: Exports were ~11% of sales in H1 FY25 (down from 13-14%); aim to maintain this ratio while growing volumes.
items.quote: Our exports in the last half year was about 11%, and previously, I think it was about 13% to 14%. We will continue to keep this level constant.

items.statement: CRGO steel sourced 80% domestically, 20% imported; tie-ups with most of the 10-15 global CRGO mills; inventory built up to cover new capacity.
items.quote: We almost have a ratio of about 80:20. 80% is domestic, and 20% is import.

items.statement: Capex for Unit II (18,000 tons) mostly complete; Unit III (leased land) could take total capacity to 25,000-30,000 tons.
items.quote: CapEx is already done in Unit II. Most of the CapEx is done. As I said, now we are ready with the capacity of 18,000 tons. We can slightly go up still in Unit II, but the expansion will happen in Unit III.

items.statement: Holds Power Grid approval up to 220 kV; executed ₹4-5 crore 400 kV order; expects 400 kV Power Grid approval in 3-4 months.
items.quote: we have already actually executed a 400 kV class order. So about, ₹4 crores to ₹5 crores of sale has already happened in the 400 kV class range. And with those precedents, and examples that were already set, we will go up to PGCIL and get it approved. So that should take about three to four months if everything goes well.

items.statement: Intends to keep debt level flat despite higher turnover; IPO proceeds fund working capital for volume growth.
items.quote: We intend to keep the debt level at the same, because when we came out with the IPO, our main objective was to fund the working capital requirement that will come with the higher volumes.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to delayed Unit II commissioning and multi-grade CRGO lead times; expects inventory to normalise by end of FY25.
items.quote: CapEx got delayed by two months. We were actually hoping to start the new facility two months back. And so because of that, we actually accumulated inventory. And now that inventory is going to get used.

items.statement: Sale prices averaged ₹300-310/kg recently; expected to rise in next 2-3 months; raw material prices at sustainable levels but direction uncertain.
items.quote: currently, our sale price on an average basis is around ₹300, ₹310. And in the near future, it will be going up in the next two to three months.

items.statement: CRGO steel prices expected to increase in short run; new supplier negotiations after December make post-December pricing uncertain
items.quote: in the short run, it will increase, because we have a fair bit of idea of the raw material prices that will, the raw material that will fall in the next one or two months.

items.statement: Targeting 30,000 ton total capacity (all three units) with peak revenue potential of ₹900 crores at full utilisation
items.quote: considering that, if we been consider theoretically full capacity utilisation of 30,000 tons, the turnover can be around ₹900 crores.

items.statement: Greenfield Unit III (6,000 tons) in planning stage; target commissioning next financial year after achieving full utilisation of Unit II
items.quote: Right now, the target is in the next financial year. Because first, our main aim will be to go up to full utilisation for Unit II

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 12-13% sustainable; 15% in H1 was due to low revenue base and volume increase
items.quote: we are hoping to target between 12% to 13%.

items.statement: Gross margin of 23% in H1 includes inventory gains; sustainable gross margin around 19-20% absent abrupt fluctuations
items.quote: Unless there is any sudden abrupt fluctuations, these margins will be continued.

items.statement: Higher voltage (400/765 kV) products fetch better margins; targeting 20-30% of capacity mix in 3 years
items.quote: In terms of capacity, I can say it will be around, it will be between 20% and 30%.

items.statement: CRGO steel consumption in India growing at 10-12% CAGR driven by government capacity addition plans till 2030
items.quote: The transformer industry continues to grow at 10% to 12%, which we feel that it will continue to grow for the next six years, at least till 2030

items.statement: Applying for PGCIL approval for 400 kV class; expecting approval within current half year (H2 FY25)
items.quote: We will be applying soon. We are expecting the approval within this half year.

items.statement: Organised players (10-12) contribute ~40-45% of market; unorganised segment has long tail of 100+ small players
items.quote: I think it would be about 40%, 45%.

items.statement: Key competitors in CRGO lamination bidding: Kryfs Power, Amod Stampings, Vardhman Stampings; Pitti Lamination operates in CRNGO (motors/alternators)
items.quote: That would be Kryfs Power, Amod Stampings, and Vardhman Stampings.

items.statement: IPO proceeds aimed at strengthening working capital to support raw material accumulation for fixed-price government contracts
items.quote: for that, we need working capital, and which was the reason we wanted to go for the public market where we can have a good strength of working capital.

items.statement: Order book includes ₹18 crores of 400 kV class orders; some customers accept orders without PGCIL approval
items.quote: our order book already has 400 kV orders. I think it was about ₹18 crores of orders that we have for 400 kV class.

items.statement: EBITDA per ton increased from ₹33.5K to ₹41.5K due to 20% volume growth and selective order picking for better capacity utilisation
items.quote: We did about 5,540 tons of CRGO steel versus last half year that was around 4,760. So that was an increase of about 19%, 20%.

items.statement: New Unit II capacity ramp-up to full utilisation expected within first half of next financial year (H1 FY26)
items.quote: We are expecting full capacity utilisation in the first half of the next financial year.

items.statement: Down cycle (2010-2020) saw receivables pressure, low capacity utilisation, and margin compression in distribution transformer segment
items.quote: We received because of receivables, capacity utilisations were not great, even for the transformer and manufacturers as well as for us.

items.statement: CRGO steel supply currently import-dependent (Germany, Poland, China, Japan, Korea); JSW Steel planning domestic CRGO production from scratch by 2027
items.quote: What JSW is planning is to make the CRGO steel from scratch in India. Probably that capacity of JSW Steel, like their earlier public disclosure that is scheduled for 2027.

items.statement: Supply transformer manufacturers across 11 kV to 765 kV classes; key customers include BHEL, Crompton Greaves, Transformers & Rectifiers
items.quote: Customers like, Bharat Heavy Electricals, Crompton Greaves, and even Transformers and Rectifiers, they make the highest range of transformers to 765 kV class.

items.statement: Discontinued CRNGO/E&I stamping capacity (motors/alternators) in last 6 months to focus on CRGO transformer cores
items.quote: We had a small capacity in CRNGO, E&I stampings, but we have discontinued that, since the last six months.

items.statement: Power transformer cores command higher margins than distribution due to stringent quality standards, high ticket sizes (₹5-25 crores), and grid-critical nature
items.quote: Power transformer players definitely fetch a better margin, because ticket size of each transformer is very high compared to distribution transformers.

items.statement: Capacity expansion will be gradual and demand-driven; machine ordering aligned with segment demand (amorphous vs CRGO distribution vs power)
items.quote: So the capacity will not be increased in one go. It will slowly and gradually be increased, which is what we did with Unit II also.

items.statement: Second half revenue expected 20% higher than first half based on 10-year pattern
items.quote: So, if you see the past 10 year 's record, our first half is always between 40 % and 45% and second-half is between 55% and 100%. So, our second-half is always 20% higher than the first half.

items.statement: Aim to maintain or improve 19% CAGR over next few years
items.quote: Therefore, I see this trend continue and I feel this Company is here. We will maintain, like you see, a CAGR is almost 19% for last 20 years and we will be able to maintain this or improve this further in the next few years.

items.statement: Expect better gross margins and pricing on FY25 contracts vs FY24
items.quote: Yes, I think it will be, in few words, it is going to be much better than this year.

items.statement: RMC gross margin expected to improve slightly or maintain at 45%
items.quote: So, what you are saying is the RMC gross margin, yes, I think it should improve a little bit. Otherwise we can maintain at this level.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 EBITDA margin 21.3%, up 19% YoY; H1 FY25 margin 21.1% vs 17.9% YoY
items.quote: The EBITDA numbers that we have achieved for this quarter is about Rs. 115 crores which itself is a growth of about 19 % on a year-on-year basis, EBITDA margins stood at 21.3% for this quarter.

items.statement: Givaudan JV targets 24% EBITDA margin with +/-2-3% range
items.quote: And as far as the products are concerned, that is going to be exclusively supplied to Givaudan and in that we are expecting an EBITDA margin of 24%, which is something which should keep us going.

items.statement: Sustainable 20%+ EBITDA margins maintained over last 6 quarters
items.quote: Over the past 6 quarters, our performance has consistently improved, driven by steadily increasing demand, improved operational efficiencies and a better product mix resulting in 21%+ EBITDA margins.

items.statement: 30% of key products contracted for 2025 with raw material back-up
items.quote: About 30% of our important products have also we have committed along with backup of raw materials for next year.

items.statement: Rs. 200-250 crore capex over 18-24 months for existing product capacity increases
items.quote: Broadly what we are talking about on the overall CAPEX required for this increase could be in the next one year for all these items, about Rs. 200-Rs. 250 crores or so in fact.

items.statement: CWIP of Rs. 233 crore includes Rs. 160 crore for PRIGIV JV, balance for Prionyl and Amber Woody Xtreme
items.quote: Basically, it is almost more than two third close to about Rs. 160 crores of the Rs. 233 crores that pertains to the PRIGIV CWIP because it has not been put to use, so that is why it is lying and capital work in progress.

items.statement: Current utilization ~80%; peak capacity 48,000-50,000 MT with Rs. 2,500-2,700 crore revenue potential
items.quote: So, the peak capacity that we had talked about is somewhere between 48,000 and 50,000 metric tons and we can generate a revenue of about close to Rs. 2,500-Rs. 2,700 crores.

items.statement: Galaxmusk, Prionyl at 75-85% utilization; Prionyl capacity to quadruple to 150 TPA
items.quote: So, now we are going to again augment the capacity and whatever we are producing is already pre -sold and as far as the capacity is concerned, it is going to go up four -folds to almost 150 tons per annum.

items.statement: Target 60,000 MT capacity via existing product augmentation and new products from QIP funds
items.quote: So, it is a culmination of various things, one definitely some of our existing products we are looking at, two with the QIP money that we are looking to raise and introduce some new products . With all that is what we had stated that we will reach about 60,000 metric tons or so.

items.statement: 60-70% of business on annual contracts; spot prices rising; Q4 FY25 and FY26 to see higher realizations
items.quote: what we do is 60% of our business is about contract, 60%-65%. We make a conscious effort to do that, 60%- 70% is the max we go. So, generally 60%-70% is low. Today also, 60%-70% of our business is almost at contract and at low prices and the balance 30 %-40% is at, maybe 20% higher prices

items.statement: US-FDA Camphor realization 25-40% higher than industrial grade
items.quote: Broadly what we see is that the realization should be anywhere between 25% and 40% higher than what we normally sell in the industry.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue mix: Pine 55%, Musk & Specialty 23%, Citral 11%, Phenol 7%, Value-added 4%
items.quote: the segment wise breakup of our revenue on the key elements , Pine contributed about 55% , Musk and Specialty is contributing about 23% of the total revenue, Citral-based aroma chemicals contribute about 11% and Phenol is about 7% and 4% coming from value added products.

items.statement: Indomeran (side-chain of Galaxmusk) to be expanded significantly this year; target among world's largest producers
items.quote: I think within this year, we will expand this capacity significantly, and we intend becoming one of the largest manufacturers of Indomeran in the world, probably one of the largest for sure , not the largest.

items.statement: Exports 63-64% (Europe, North America); domestic 36-37%; customers' turnover up 10% driving demand
items.quote: Exports contribute about 64%, led by Europe and North America. And of course, India is also the contributor of about 36% of our revenue.

items.statement: Givaudan JV exclusive for 42 specialty products; 51% Privi, 49% Givaudan; land bank expanded pre-launch
items.quote: The first thing is that we should be proud that as Indians, Global Fortune 500 giant has relied on us to be their technology partners with Priv i having 51% and they having 49% and they have Speciality products which they have been manufacturing for nearly 80 years . They have transferred those products to India and it is going to be manufactured in the JV plant.

items.statement: India largest Camphor producer; Chinese competition; few Indian peers with US-FDA Camphor listing
items.quote: There are a few Indian companies who have also registered as a key pharma ingredient i n the US-FDA space. And we are the latest to join on the bandwagon and China of late, yes have been competing with all. India is the largest Camphor manufacturers in fact.

items.statement: US-FDA listing achieved for Camphor (ingredient, not API); pharma qualification process underway
items.quote: See to reiterate, it is a listing of our product in the US-FDA, which means that my Camphor is not an end bulk drug . It is only an ingredient which can be used in making formulation.

items.statement: Other expenses up 50% due to higher export volumes, freight costs from Iran-Israel conflict
items.quote: If you basically see, the volume has increased in this quarter and the other expenses forms , the selling and distribution expenses are with higher volume of sale happening around. We also end up having that much of units being exported , so freight expenses ha ve also gone up. And the Iran-Israel dispute has also slightly increased the freight expenses.

items.statement: Term loan repayments on schedule; all bank obligations repaid; target debt/EBITDA below 2x
items.quote: Debt repayment anyway, the term loan repayment is happening as per its schedule and that goes around because whatever CAPEXes we have done using bank money, there are certain repayment obligations. And you would have seen even in our current financials, we have repaid all the bank obligation.

items.statement: QIP timeline to be announced by bankers at appropriate time
items.quote: We will be in a position to answer through our bankers at the appropriate time.

items.statement: Acquisition progress confidential; bankers to inform when ready
items.quote: The bankers will inform you at the appropriate time when we are ready for it in fact.

items.statement: R&D team of 91 people; 33% each on capacity intensification, new products, PRIGIV/specialties
items.quote: So, I would really boast over here that we have a great R&D team. We have almost 91 people working around the clock. So, I think for the Company, which is few thousand crores, 91 is a very good resource to have.

items.statement: Global aroma chemicals addressable market estimated $6-8 billion; India, Brazil, Indonesia, Middle East key growth geographies
items.quote: I would say aroma chemicals and aroma. It could be between $6 and $8 billion , I think so . I cannot put a number because there is no. It could be in that range.

items.statement: Camphor prices volatile monthly (Rs. 415-500/kg); secured raw material mitigates risk
items.quote: Honestly speaking, I am saying, it changes almost every month, sometimes it is high, sometimes it is low, sometimes high season, low season. So, every time the price, I cannot, I don't know, maybe Rs 450, sometimes Rs 500, some Rs 415.

items.statement: Strides reaffirms FY25 EBITDA guidance of INR 950-1,000 crore including OneSource and INR 750-800 crore excluding OneSource, trending towards higher end
items.value: INR 950-1,000 crore (incl. OneSource); INR 750-800 crore (excl. OneSource)
items.quote: we're very confident of hitting our stated objective of INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores, including OneSource, and taking off OneSource business, we are very confident of hitting the INR750 crores to INR800 crores EBITDA range.

items.statement: OneSource guided at $160-180 million revenue with 34% EBITDA margin, H1 EBITDA positive, targeting $59-60 million EBITDA with $20 million exit quarter run rate
items.quote: we're now guiding for $160 million to $180 million with a 34% EBITDA margin. Please understand that this H1 from Stelis has been EBITDA positive, but it's still a PAT loss. That would change si gnificantly in Q3 and Q4 as we start commercializing our GLPs

items.statement: OneSource revenue guidance of $350-400 million over next 3-4 years with exit EBITDA near 40%

items.statement: US revenue target of $400 million by FY27-28 reaffirmed with margin discipline

items.statement: Net debt-to-EBITDA tracking ahead of <2x guidance for FY25, currently at 2.1x
items.quote: I'm very happy that we are tracking ahead of our net debt to EBITDA guidance of less than two for FY '25.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to remain 17-20% for FY25
items.quote: Our effec tive tax rate at 17% is in line with our estimates, and we expect it to remain in this range of 17% to 20% for '25

items.statement: US business trending ahead of run rate with $75 million revenue, driven by Endo portfolio relaunches and market share gains
items.quote: Pleasing, of course, was our outstanding US performance. We are trending ahead of our run rate. We had $75 million of revenue this year. items.statement: Other regulated markets 3-4% short of target growth rate, with tepid Continental Europe performance offset by strong UK and Australia

items.statement: New markets (Africa, access, APAC, MENA) growing steadily but subscale, expected to be star performers in coming years
items.quote: The new markets that we have been focusing on is growing steadily. And this is a new -- these are new markets that we have seeded and includes the African region where we have a branded strategy, the access markets and new regions of APAC and MENA. They continue to grow.

items.statement: Gross margin target 59-60%, Q2 saw 75 bps sequential decline due to higher access market mix and lower Europe sales
items.quote: we are in that 59%, 60%, that is our target range. Like we said, we had a slightly elevated access market business and a lower European sale. That's why we had a tad 75 bps reduction this quarter.

items.statement: H1 EBITDA INR 452 crore at ~45-47% of full year guidance range
items.quote: EBITDA at INR452 crores is almost 45%, 47% of our range, and we're very confident of hitting our stated objective of INR950 crores to INR1,000 crores

items.statement: OneSource fully sold out on capacity, commercializing liraglutide GLP from Q4, backordered with customers forecasting higher volumes
items.quote: We currently are fully sold out with our capacities. We are commercializing the liraglutide GLP starting from Q4. And we are backordered as some of our customers have forecasted significantl y lower volumes

items.statement: OneSource win ratio ~40% on RFPs, strong order book with annualized exit run rate of $80 million
items.quote: Our win ratio now is about 40%, which is quite a good number for a new CDMO player. And that is a pleasing number for us to share with you today.

items.quote: This assumes a capex of approximately $100 million that will be required for -- required that will be a combination of customer advances, the $50 million that we will invest and also the free cash that the business will generate once the merger is completed.

items.statement: H1 capex spend INR 92 crore funded by strong operating cash flow of INR 418 crore
items.quote: our capex spend of INR92 crores in H1. With this strong operating cash generation, our debt is also reduced.

items.statement: 71 commercialized US products (2 new approvals, 1 new + 3 from dormant list of 60 products)
items.quote: We now have one additional product where we are market leaders during the quarter in the US, and we now have -- we have increased our commercialized products to 71, two new products approved and one new product approved and three from our dormant product list that we have identified 60 products that meet our criteria

items.statement: Onboarded world's largest softgel consumer as first CDMO customer, multiyear contract ramping to ~1 billion units in 2.5-3 years
items.quote: we have already onboarded one of the world's largest consumers of soft gelatins as our first customer and with commercial shipments starting from this year. items.statement: OneSource softgel revenue split ~50/50 Strides vs third-party, all incremental growth from third parties
items.quote: We have guided earlier. It's about half and half and we stay with that, but there's no incremental growth coming from Strides. All new contracts are only with third parties.

items.statement: Cash-to-cash cycle improved to 126 days, H1 operating cash flow INR 418 crore on EBITDA INR 453 crore
items.quote: we have seen further improvement in our cash to cash cycle, which is now at 126 days. This has significantly helped us generate operating cash despite a very significant degrowth that we had during this quarter. On an H1 EBITDA of INR453 crores, we have generated cash flow from operations of INR418 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduced INR 133 crore in H1 to INR 1,902 crore, net debt/EBITDA 2.1x, targeting net cash by FY27 after OneSource merger and $300 crore debt pushdown
items.quote: Our net debt at INR1,902 crores is a reduction of INR133 crores in H1. With this reduction, our Net Debt-to-EBITDA ratio is at 2.1x. And I'm very happy that we are tracking ahead of our net debt to EBITDA guidance of less than two for FY '25.

items.statement: OneSource capital raise released ~$700 million to Strides shareholders, $95 million proceeds for debt reduction including bridge loans
items.quote: We've had a great response for our capital raise and we've got, we're very delighted to have marquee investors on our cap table at OneSource. This has also led in releasing close to about $700 million to Strides

items.statement: NCLT process for OneSource merger on track, positive outcome expected before end of calendar year, listing within 60 days after order
items.quote: On the NCLT process, we are on track. We hope to have the NC LT a positive outcome, obviously, subject to regulatory approvals and the compliances that are required for us to get an NCLT order in place. We expect news -- positive news before the end of this calendar year

items.statement: ROCE improved to 17.2% from 12.8% at end of FY24
items.quote: Our all-round performance is also reflecting in the ROCE metric, has now improved to 17.2% from 12.8% that we ended in FY '24.

items.statement: Biosecurity Act driving significant new RFP interest and customer engagement for OneSource drug substance capabilities
items.quote: Overall, we are superbly excited with the number of RFPs that we have been issuing, especially post the Biosecurity Act, and we have very pleasing response to our drug substance capabilities.

items.statement: FY25 pre-IndAS EBITDA guidance of Rs 120 crore

items.quote: We targeted pre -IndAS EBITDA of 120 crores. I think PAT is 55% of that. So , it should be about 60-65 crores.

items.quote: we always guide that we want to reach 10% pre-IndAS EBITDA levels in the next 2 to 3 years.

items.quote: I think for H2 our target is around 15% to 20%.

items.quote: If you talk about, yes total revenues, the revenue growth should be more than 30%-35%.

items.quote: The CAPEX required is Rs. 1,000 per square feet. So, for a 10,000 square feet store it's 1 crore.

items.quote: The Company added 22 net stores during the first half of the year, taking our total store count to 139 stores. We have added another 5 stores during the current quarter taking the current store count to 144 stores.

items.statement: Robust festive demand; high double-digit SSSG and footfall growth continuing into October
items.quote: We have seen robust demand in the ongoing Festive Season, and we are very hopeful that the ensuing wedding season and the winter season will further strengthen our position.

items.statement: Macro still negative; growth driven by internal strength not external uptick
items.quote: I would say the macroeconomic factors are still a bit negative. Even if you look at the results that have come out in consumer durables and FMCG companies it's not that promising.
