items.statement: Fixed cost leverage drives EBITDA margin expansion; 10% SSSG yields 18-19% profit growth
items.quote: So, most of our costs are fixed cost. It's the fixed cost business where variable cost is a very small proportion of total cost. So, even if we increase our sales by 10%, you are essentially increasing profitability by 18%-19%.

items.statement: Markup only 55%; 91% full-price sales in H1 FY25 vs 85% last year
items.quote: if you sell products at the margin that we sell which is best in the industry, it's only a 55% markup and we are selling 91% of our products at full price then the sky is the limit.

items.statement: 3,200 designs/SKUs per store; four attributes (design, fabric, color, fit) drive assortment
items.quote: at any given point of time at any of our stores there are 3,200 designs and 3,200 SKUs. So, it's all about assortment.

items.statement: Target customers earning Rs 10,000-80,000/month covering 80% of India
items.quote: The customers that we're targeting is anyone who earns between Rs. 10,000 a month to almost Rs. 70,000-80,000 a month. So, that covers almost 80% of India.

items.statement: No significant impact from Zudio; ASP Rs 260-270 vs Zudio >500; different customer class
items.quote: we haven't seen any sort of significant impact due to Zudio opening because our ASP is Rs. 260-270 whereas Zudio's ASP exceeds 500. So , the customer class is different.

items.statement: No debt for store expansion; CC limit used for vendor bill discounting only
items.quote: No, it will be through internal accruals and even that the debt that we have on our books is essentially for bill discounting. So , our vendors have a facility where they can take payments and they can discount their bills whenever they want.

items.statement: No QIP or fundraise planned; feel undervalued; may consider at Rs 1,200 sq ft and 25% ROE
items.quote: No, we're not thinking on those lines because of course like when you grow at that pace it comes with an added bit of risk. items.quote: We have almost a 40-to-50-member team and all the crucial people have been given retention bonuses and they are all linked to the profitability of the Company. They all have incentives also that is linked to their targets.

items.statement: Expects electricity demand to grow ~7% annually for next 7-8 years, driving exchange volume growth
items.quote: And I'm sure the projections are, the demand for electricity is going to increase at a rate of almost about 7% for the next seven, eight years.

items.quote: Power demand at 435 billion units in Q2 was largely flat at plus 0.5% Y-o-Y with a peak demand of 227 gigawatts. However, in the first six months of FY '25, power demand was higher by 5.6% over the previous year.

items.quote: We recorded a total trading volume of 36.7 billion units in this quarter with a growth of 38.2% on year-on-year basis. For the first half of FY '25, IEX traded volume of 67 billion units, a growth of 30% over the same period in FY '24.

items.statement: RTM volumes up 31% YoY to ~11 BU in Q2 FY25; RTM share in product mix increased to ~30% from 27% at end FY24
items.quote: For Q2 FY '25, RTM volumes were higher by 31% Y-o-Y at nearly 11 billion units, showcasing its critical role in developing Discoms and open access consumer efficiently manage short-term electricity needs.

items.statement: Green market volumes rose 246% YoY to ~2.6 BU in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Similarly, for the quarter, Green market volumes rose to 246% to nearly 2.6 billion units as compared with Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: REC volumes jumped 277% YoY to 63 lakh certificates in Q2 FY25 after fee reduction
items.quote: In Q2, a total of 63 lakhs certificates were traded, a jump of 277% over the same quarter last fiscal.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew 26.2% YoY to INR167.8 cr; PAT grew 25.2% YoY to INR108.3 cr in Q2 FY25
items.quote: On a consolidated basis, revenue for the company grew 26.2% on year-on-year basis in Q2 FY '25, increasing to INR167.8 crores from INR133 crores in Q2 FY '24. items.statement: Reduced REC transaction fee from INR20 to INR10 per certificate per side effective 12 Aug 2024 due to lower REC prices
items.quote: Consequent to reduction in REC prices, we revised our transaction fee on RECs from INR20 per certificate to INR10 per certificate on either side of transaction with effect from 12th August, 2024.

items.statement: Electricity transaction fee unchanged at 2 paise per unit per side since 2011 despite clearing prices rising from ~INR2.5 to ~INR5
items.quote: In case of electricity, our transaction fees is continuing at two-paise on either-side right from 2011 when the electricity rates were almost about 2.5, 3rupees. Today, electricity clearing price is almost in the range of INR5. In spite of that, we have not increased the transaction fees.

items.statement: CERC draft proposes standardizing TAM products across exchanges to improve liquidity; IEX expects to be larger beneficiary
items.quote: So CE RC has now decided to streamline this activity, and there will be standard products available in the market so that buyers and sellers can see what is available for the sell and what is what they want to buy. And I think this is a very good initiative of the CERC and it is good for the market.

items.statement: Deviation Settlement Mechanism 2024 narrows deviation band for solar/wind to 10%, expected to increase RTM volumes
items.quote: With regards solar and wind generators. deviation percentage allowed for levy has been narrowed to 10%. This is expected to further increase RTM volumes at exchanges.

items.statement: LPSC amendment mandates central generating stations to offer un-requisitioned power on exchanges; ~100 MU/day coming, 15-20 MU/day clearing
items.quote: As a result, about 100 million units of URS power from central generating stations is coming to the exchange platform, out of which 15 million to 20 million unit is getting cleared on daily business.

items.statement: Gujarat ERC introduced penalty up to INR3.72/unit for RPO shortfall, expected to support REC market
items.quote: In the event an obligated entity does not fulfill its renewal purchase obligation and also doe s not purchase the certificates, the Commission has introduced payment of traditional penalty up to INR3.72 per unit for shortfall in the specified renewable energy consumption

items.statement: RTM share increased to nearly 30% of overall product mix over last two quarters from 27% at end FY24
items.quote: The share of RTM in our overall product mix has also increased to nearly 30% over the last two quarters from 27% at the end FY '24.

items.quote: We continue to await approval from CRC for our long duration contracts. We have already filed a petition with them for approval of 11-month contract on which the hearing has happened and order is reserved. Further, we have filed petition with CERC for approval of Green RTM segment.

items.quote: We are happy to inform that our wholly-owned subsidiary, International Carbon Exchange has been accredited as India's first renewal energy certificate issuer. items.statement: Coal exchange launch dependent on government approval; after approval, 6-8 months to operationalize

items.quote: EPR trading also draft regulations have been issued and we have received the public comments. They are in the process of finalizing the regulations. Once the regulations are finalized, then they will appoint the agency for t he purpose of EPR trading

items.quote: On buy si de, 100% of the distribution companies of the country are registered with us. Industrial consumers, we have more than 4,500 large industries, they are all registered with us

items.statement: Exchange prices provide enough arbitrage for BESS to be commercially viable at current prices

items.statement: Market coupling unlikely to happen; if it does, IEX has ways to retain market share
items.quote: I'm very sure coupling is not going to happen. So let us not worry about that. And in case coupling happens, we have ways and means to ensure that we are able to retain our market share.

items.statement: CERC discussion paper on transaction fee global best practices (per Apr 2023 order) has not progressed; no timeline specified
items.quote: April '23 order did not specify any timeline for the discussion paper. So as of now, to our knowledge, nothing has happened and nothing is happening on that.

items.statement: Top 3 priorities for next 4-5 years: deepen electricity market with new products & policy advocacy; grow gas exchange volumes; pursue diversification (coal exchange, EPR trading)
items.quote: One is electricity exchange, continue to introduce more products on this and do business development activities, policy advocacy so that we are able to deepen this market. items.statement: Branch network expanded to 2,031 across 398 districts; added 55 new branches in Q2 FY25

items.quote: Going forward as well, Praveen, the sale to external will be very low. We will be providing resin only to select customers who really need.

items.statement: Competitive intensity increasing but industry growing at 15%+ CAGR over next 5-10 years; brand premium and quality differentiation maintained

items.quote: Working capital was slightly higher during H1 FY '25 at 176 days. We had indicated in our previous calls on increased receivables days. We have also been required to build up some levels of inventory in order to meet the delay in order servicing of Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Company remains net debt free with INR446 crores cash and equivalents as of Sep 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain a net debt free company, and I'm happy to inform you that we have generated strong cash flow from operations of INR 134 crores in the first half of FY '25, with cash and cash equivalents of INR446 crores on the books as of 30th September 2024.

items.statement: Chinese players aggressive on commodity API pricing but limited impact as <20% business in emerging markets
items.quote: The Chinese players are being extremely aggressive in offering prices in the market . Again, for us, it has a much lesser impact . So because less than 20% of our business is in the emerging markets, where the regulatory framework is not

items.statement: Biosecure Act expected to benefit Indian CDMO companies including Glenmark Life Sciences
items.quote: Biosecure Act is certainly going to help us. Indian companies in general. And we are seeing that sort of wind blowing in this direction.

items.statement: Q4 CDMO project start may slip to H1 FY26 due to regulatory approval uncertainty
items.quote: From Q4, it may get pushed out into first half of next year because it's all driven by regulators, I mean, we don't really control anything there, neither does the customer really.

items.statement: Capacity constraints may require dropping low-margin ROW business in H2 FY25
items.quote: If we are seeing that we are capacity constrained, we may let go some ROW business with lower margin. So that -- if that does happen, unfortunately, I mean, we try not to let that happen.

items.statement: CDMO base business (3 projects) lumpy with servicing issues; one project added indication but slow pickup
items.quote: On the CDMO base business, which is on 3 projects, we've always sort of cautioned that this is a lumpy business. The demand go up and down. And some of our servicing issues have also impacted the CDMO business.

items.statement: New CDMO discussions ongoing but no commitments; selection process long and unpredictable
items.quote: There is a few CDMO projects that we are in discussions. We haven't locked in anything yet. But again, what happens is that once a decision is made is when we know that, yes, okay, we got selected.

items.statement: High potency pipeline expects 10-11 molecules to commercialize over next 2-5 years
items.quote: We expect a good 7, 8 molecules to sort of commercialize in the next 2 to 5 years. So there will be a pretty good hit rate on the high potent pipeline. In fact, no, on onco, it will be about 7 to 8 molecules, and there'll be another 3 to 4 molecules on the HP API, non-onco, high potent. So we are looking at about 11 -- 10 to 11 molecules that would commercialize.

items.statement: Reaffirmed 30% revenue growth target for FY25
items.quote: Absolutely. So, if you look at it, traditionally we have about 45% of our revenue coming from the first half and 55% from the second. And going by the current trend, if we look at it, we are looking to meet our aggressive target and sustain the 30% growth that we have already shown in the first half.

items.statement: Capex target for FY25 is Rs 100 crore, with Rs 60 crore planned for H1 FY26
items.quote: So, the CAPEX guidance of Rs. 160 crores, as we had explained in the earlier call also, is divided into two parts where we had kept Rs. 100 crores for the current financial year and Rs. 60 crores in the first half of the next financial year.

items.statement: Incurred Rs 94.3 crore capex in H1 FY25, highest ever
items.quote: In the current year, the Company has already undertaken a CAPEX of Rs. 94.30 crores, which is the highest ever in the Company's history.

items.statement: Depreciation expected around Rs 36-37 crore for FY25
items.quote: And so that would lead to about Rs. 36 crores, Rs. 37 crores of depreciation for the whole financial year, the way we see it right now. It could even be anywhere around Rs. 1 crore or Rs. 2 crores higher than that.

items.statement: Order book at Rs 104 crore as of Oct 1, 2024, up 31% YoY, fully executable in FY25
items.quote: The Company has a very healthy order book at Rs. 104 crores as on the 1st of October 2024, which is a 31% year-on-year growth and this entire Rs. 104 crores order book is executable in the current financial year itself.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 35% for H1 FY25, seen as sustainable
items.quote: So, we are currently at 35% for the half year and we see that as the sustainable level going forward.

items.statement: Equipment rental EBITDA margin at 50-51% in H1, targeting 53-55% sustainable
items.quote: So, we have been operating right now in the 50% to 51% EBITDA margins, and those should be at least around 53% to 55% as we keep stabilizing this with our CAPEX coming into play.

items.statement: Warehousing & transportation EBITDA margin expected to return to 22-23% in H2
items.quote: But they are stabilizing now, so we do see that the margins will rise again and be at a stable level of where we usually operate at about 22% to 23%.

items.statement: Seeing aggressive expansion in cement and steel sectors, demand robust for equipment rental
items.quote: Rather, on the contrary, we are seeing aggressive expansion across both the main sectors that we are working with, the cement and steel, where the demand is still pretty robust for at least the equipment that they need in our rental division.

items.statement: Crane rental utilization at 78% in Q2, targeting above 85% in H2
items.quote: The utilization level for Q2 was about at 78%.

items.statement: Fleet includes 300+ machines, largest crane 800 tons acquired July 2024
items.quote: On the equipment rental front, the Company has more than 300 machines. The largest capacity crane in the Company's fleet is of 800 tons capacity, which has been acquired in July 2024 as a brand new fully loaded machine from Zoomlion China.

items.statement: Average monthly rental yield 2.96% in H1 FY25 vs 2.75% YoY, net yield ~1.7-1.75%
items.quote: In the equipment rental segment, the average monthly rental yield was at 2.96% for the half year ended September '24, rising from 2.75% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Rental yields expected to trend upward in H2 with demand pickup and capex stabilization
items.quote: So, with the CAPEX that we have already executed and now things are stabilizing post monsoons and picking up with the kind of demand that is there, and the pricing that we are seeing in the market, we do see an upward trend to the rental yields, and that should take us to a better position going forward.

items.statement: Receivable days improved to 85 days as of Sep 30, 2024 from 100 days YoY
items.quote: The Company has been seeing that the receivable days have been coming down, as we saw that these receivable days are at 85 days as of 30th September, '24, compared to 100 days in the similar period last year.

items.statement: No immediate debt increase planned; may consider in Q4 depending on situation
items.quote: Nothing planned as such for an immediate increase on the debt side. We will consider that probably in Q4 as we understand the situation, because we have already done a considerable amount of our CAPEX that we were supposed to do.

items.statement: Warehousing segment volumes impacted by labor issues at Vizag Steel in Q1, now stabilizing
items.quote: Because if you would see, in last financial year, for the first half itself we had executed 3.88 Million Tons of steel, and in this first half we have only done 3.4 Million Tons of steel.

items.statement: Entered renewable energy sector (solar & wind) in FY25, currently ~5% of order book
items.quote: In the current financial year, the Company has also entered the renewable energy sector, covering both the solar and wind energy domains.

items.statement: Cash PAT grew 38% YoY to Rs 30.08 crore in H1 FY25
items.quote: And it was complemented by a cash PAT of Rs. 30.08 crores, which again is a 38% increase on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Equipment rental revenue grew 54% YoY to Rs 52.2 crore in H1 FY25 with 50% EBITDA margin
items.quote: For the half year-ended 30th September, '24, our equipment rental segment registered a high growth of 54% in revenue at Rs. 52.2 crores and recorded an EBITDA of 50%.

items.statement: Hiring external cranes at 15-20% margin to fulfill package contracts, temporarily pressuring Segment-A PBT margin
items.quote: So, it is basically like an aggregating kind of a model, so that was higher in the 2nd Quarter which has led to the expense side going high because they come up with a margin of only about 15% to 20% if it is a decent size crane.
